title: Microsoft Purview DLP: delegate Copilot and Cowork policies to administrative units
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a PowerShell parameter for assigning administrative units to DLP policies, contrary to the briefing's automation gap. The delegation description also omits Entra roles taking precedence over scoped Purview assignments, and the licensing list expands a subscription name incorrectly.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: DLP is extending administrative unit support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention is extending Administrative Units support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork.

claims.claim: Organizations can delegate supported Copilot DLP policy management to administrators within assigned units without tenant-wide policy-management permissions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: Policy unit scoping is at Microsoft Purview portal > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units.
claims.quote: go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy ... On the Admin units page, select the administrative units for the policy.

claims.claim: Role-group member unit assignment is at Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users > Assign admin units.
claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups. ... Select Select. ... select the users or groups and select Assign admin units.
claims.fix: The printed labels are correct but omit the intermediate member-selection sequence. Keep the path and add to its note: 'After Choose users, select the users, select Select, then select those members and choose Assign admin units.'

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose; Open questions
claims.claim: No automation or PowerShell administrative-unit parameter is documented for scoping a Copilot DLP policy.
claims.quote: The PolicyRBACScopes parameter specifies the administrative units to assign to the policy. A valid value is the Microsoft Entra ObjectID (GUID value) of the administrative unit.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to kind 'powershell', call 'New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy-name> -PolicyRBACScopes <administrative-unit-GUIDs>', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-dlpcompliancepolicy'. Replace the portal-only and missing-parameter prose with 'Security & Compliance PowerShell documents New-DlpCompliancePolicy -PolicyRBACScopes for assigning administrative units to a DLP policy; values are Entra object GUIDs, separated by commas.' Remove the open question asking whether any PowerShell equivalent is planned.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No documented automation assigns administrative units to individual Purview role-group members, and Add-RoleGroupMember has no unit parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview assign administrative units role group member PowerShell; Purview administrative units PowerShell role; Purview role group member administrative units Graph API assignment. Opened purview-permissions, purview-admin-units, Add-RoleGroupMember and Set-RoleGroup; no matching operation.

claims.claim: Policy scope follows the user submitting the prompt, not the accessed file or email's owner.

claims.claim: A Finance-scoped policy applies to Finance users interacting with content owned outside Finance.
claims.quote: a policy scoped to the Finance administrative unit applies to Finance users' Copilot and Cowork interactions, even when they access content owned by someone outside Finance.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Assigning units makes a member restricted, with effective reach determined by Purview role-group membership and unit assignment.
claims.quote: If you assign both an Entra role and a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment ... the Entra role takes precedence at runtime. As a result, the user's effective permissions are unscoped
claims.fix: Qualify the categorical assignment and reach statements, including controls[1].note, with: 'For overlapping capabilities, an Entra role takes precedence over a scoped Purview role-group assignment and leaves effective access unscoped.' Replace the last clause in Why it matters with 'because effective reach depends on Purview role-group membership, unit assignment and any overriding Entra role.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.

claims.quote: Before you create a scoped policy, configure administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID and assign them to the appropriate Microsoft Purview role group members.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: The new unit-scoping feature leaves Copilot DLP rule actions unchanged.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot administrative unit DLP default optional existing policies unchanged actions. Opened Copilot DLP learn-about, purview-admin-units and dlp-policy-reference; sources describe scoping and continued existing policies, not an explicit guarantee that rule actions are unchanged.
claims.fix: Remove 'The policy actions themselves, such as preventing Copilot from processing prompts, are unchanged' and 'they do not change what a Copilot DLP rule does'. Keep the documented description that administrative units narrow policy management and investigation scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot DLP policies can prevent processing sensitive prompts and thereby restrict a user's interaction.
claims.quote: This policy prevents Copilot and Cowork from returning a response when prompts contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated default behaviour beyond existing tenant-wide policies continuing and scoping being optional.
claims.quote: Unrestricted administrators don't have to select administrative units as part of the policy configuration. They can keep the default of the entire directory or select one or more administrative units.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of the second paragraph in Why it matters with 'Using administrative units is optional; unrestricted administrators can keep the default of the entire directory, and existing tenant-wide policies continue to apply.' This agrees with admin-opt-in without asserting an undocumented default gap.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells administrators to configure or review has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Define the administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID ... Review alerts and Activity explorer ... Revisit unit membership ... Table rows cover policy scoping and role-group member assignment only.
claims.fix: The checklist's Entra unit creation/membership and alerts/Activity explorer review steps have no matching table rows. To keep the correction within existing rows, remove those three checklist bullets rather than add new controls.
